EXTANT COPIES—The only issues known to have been preserved are the eight copies loaned the author—one by Mrs. V. E. Conway, of Leonard, Texas, one by Judge Lee A. Clark, of Greenville, Texas, and one by Mr. J. W. Hunt, of Rockbridge, Texas. These are the issues for April 20, October 1, November 1, November 20, December 1, 1884; January 1, April 1, June 8, and November 1, of 1885. Exact facsimile photostats of these eight papers are now being preserved in the Archives of the Texas State Library in the Capitol Building.

THE EDITORS—The editorial and business staff of the Messenger was chosen from representatives of societies elected by the Platonian Society at the end of each half year. The College's official advertisement, which appears in 1887 seems to have offered only the opportunity to L. W. Pierce as business manager. The editorial staff included:

J. P. Atteberry, Senior Editor
J. C. Atteberry, Junior Editor
E. L. Treiber, Local Editor

At its meeting on April 17 the Society seriously considered a proposal to elect a complete editorial staff of young ladies, in recognition of the interest shown by women as contributors. It finally elected this group, however:

This new staff was to begin work with the May issue. Under the direction of Prof. J. T. Ashcraft, the new teacher from Alabama, the business and editorial staff of the editors were:

L. W. Pierce, Senior Editor
L. W. Pierce, Senior Editor
J. C. Treiber, Junior Editor
C. E. Phillips, Local Editor
